Mr. Manoj Bhatt, learned Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand.
2. The present Bail Application has been filed
by the applicant, who is in judicial custody in
connection with Case Crime No. 87 of 2026,
registered at Police Station Piran Kaliyar, District
Haridwar, for the offences punishable under
Sections 115(2), 117(2), 118(2), 351(2), 351(3) and
352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits
that the incident arose out of an altercation between
the families of the applicant and the complainant,
who are the sons of real brothers. It is contended
that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the
present case on account of the existing family
dispute. The specific allegation against the applicant
is that he assaulted the injured person with an iron
knuckle duster, resulting in a fracture of the nasal

UKHC010125272026
2026:UHC:9272
bone.
5. It is further submitted that the applicant has
also lodged a complaint against the complainant in
respect of the same incident and, therefore, cross-cases have arisen out of the same occurrence.
Learned counsel further submits that the incident
was captured on CCTV footage, a copy of which
has been filed by the State along with its counter-affidavit. According to learned counsel, the CCTV
footage does not clearly establish the involvement
of the applicant in the alleged assault, which is
stated to be inconsistent with the version of the
alleged eyewitness.
6. Per contra, learned State Counsel has
opposed the bail application.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant further
submits that, vide order dated 09.09.2026, a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court granted short-term bail
to the applicant for a period of six weeks on the
ground that he had participated in the selection
examination for the post of Personal
Assistant/Stenographer and his name appeared in
the provisional merit list. It is further submitted that
the aforesaid period of short-term bail has not yet
expired and, therefore, the applicant may be
permitted not to surrender during the subsistence of
the said order.
8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties
and upon perusal of the material available on
record, this Court finds that the incident arose out of

UKHC010125272026
2026:UHC:9272
a dispute between two related families and that
cross-cases have been lodged in respect of the same
occurrence. Further, upon consideration of the
CCTV footage placed on record by the State, the
alleged involvement of the applicant does not
appear to be clearly established from the footage.
9. Considering the overall facts and
circumstances of the case, without expressing any
opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of
the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged
on bail. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
10. Since the applicant is already on short-term
bail granted vide order dated 09.09.2026, and the
period thereof has not yet expired, he need not
surrender pursuant to the said order. He shall be
released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond
and two reliable sureties, each in the like amount, to
the satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to
compliance with the conditions imposed by the
court concerned.
11. All pending applications, if any, stand
disposed of.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
